extracted.intended_audience: comedians, comedy writers, and creators working in filmed/musical comedy (fans/students of Bo Burnham's craft)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and producing comedy intended for recorded/filmed formats (especially musical and visually-driven pieces), with emphasis on medium-specific choices, meta-awareness, joke density, and tonal range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-content equation / form must earn its keep
rubrics_metrics.description: The form of the joke must do something the content alone can't. Ask: what does THIS medium let me do that another wouldn't?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the medium to add meaning the words alone cannot: a song allows you to MEAN two things at once (lyrics + music); a camera move can underline a joke a microphone can't. Always evaluate whether another medium would do this better; if not, the form is earning its keep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-awareness used sparingly (tool not pretense)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comic acknowledging the comic is a tool: it cuts through pretense. But meta-awareness used too often becomes its own pretense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy meta/self-awareness rarely so it stays effective — 'once per show, not once per joke.' Watch for overuse that signals self-consciousness rather than insight. When scoring, penalize repetitive self-referential moves that call attention to the device rather than the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: High joke density / avoid dead air
rubrics_metrics.description: Inside packs jokes per minute at roughly 3x the rate of conventional stand-up specials; keep density high and remove any moment the audience could disengage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use editing to eliminate lulls; replace traditional verbal setups with visual information; allow songs to function as both setup and punch. Evaluate pacing by assessing jokes-per-minute and whether there's any 'dead air' where attention can drop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use visuals to replace words where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Are visuals replacing words where they can? Visual information should stand in for setups or exposition when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor visual setups (camera moves, framing, staging) over explanatory lines when the image can carry the idea. Score pieces higher when the visual grammar does double duty (establishes context and delivers comedic payoff) and when editing choices keep the visual flow tight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit recorded/filmed media to allow tonal range
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the piece allow tonal range a single live audience couldn't sustain? Recorded media permits tonal shifts and forms stand-up cannot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that live performance imposes rhythmic and tonal constraints ('the room contracts the comic'). For filmed work, intentionally use editing, sound, and camera to move between tones (comic, tragic, contemplative) that might feel uneasy or incoherent onstage. Reward pieces that purposefully leverage recording to expand tonal possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve the work, not the audience's affection
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you in service of the work, not the audience's affection?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize structural, tonal, and formal choices that strengthen the piece even if they risk immediate audience approval. Penalize pandering or obvious crowd-pleasing choices that undercut the work's integrity. Consider whether choices were made to preserve the performer’s likability versus to realize the artistic goal.
